text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former finance minister Emmanuel Kasonde has rejoined the ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD). He left the party after being sacked by President Frederick Chiluba in 1993.
- Chiluba has pledged $100,000 to the Organisation of African Unity's special drought and famine emergency assistance fund.
- The Economic Association of Zambia has suggested that the European Union channel its aid through local commercial banks rather than the government, to ensure easier access by Zambian entrepreneurs.
- Police in the central town of Kabwe have caught three people accused of involvement in a growing Satanist cult.
- Workers at university teaching hospitals have called off a strike over pay increases.

- President Chiluba has awarded judges a pay increase of 207 percent, in what opposition leaders say is an attempt to influence their deliberations in an electoral petition challenging his presidency.
